tasks.short: Arrange meetings, collaborate with colleagues in team meetings and informal talks on teaching and research issues, work on shared course and research documents, write action points, and circulate them.

steps.what: Colleagues mark their free times in the scheduling poll
Nursing instructor finds a meeting time with colleagues: by e-mail rounds today, by a scheduling poll after the change
Nursing instructor collaborates with colleagues in meetings to address teaching and research issues
Nursing instructor discusses issues with colleagues informally
Nursing instructor works on shared course and research documents by e-mailing versions
Nursing instructor writes the action points in the short template on the team page
Nursing instructor checks the final action points: each action, owner and date says what the meeting agreed
Nursing instructor shares the checked action points with the team from the team page

tasks.design: Meeting times come from a scheduling poll in the shared calendar ({CALENDAR}). Course and research documents live in one shared document space ({DOCS}) with versions and comments instead of e-mailed copies. The instructor writes action points in a short template on the team page, checks them and shares them once with the team from there. Meetings and talks with colleagues stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Times were found by e-mail rounds and documents went back and forth as attachments.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared calendars and document spaces are standard in universities.
tasks.still_hard: Clinical schedules make shared meeting times rare.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the compromise between two colleagues who teach the same topic differently.
tasks.altitude: Less e-mailing of times and versions; meetings and talks stay.

evidence.claim: Shared calendars, scheduling polls and document spaces with versions are standard office tools.

assumptions: Boundary: from open issues to action points shared; carrying out the actions is outside.
Input contract: team page and document space set up by the department; fallback is e-mail.
Meetings and informal talks do not change.

Colleagues use the shared space as they would e-mail; their poll answers are shown in s0. s4 keeps 60 for writing in the shared documents; s5 keeps 90 because the template gives only the layout; s6 keeps 30 for sharing.
research_questions: Do fewer versions of the same document circulate?

incremental.description: Nursing instructor tidies the shared document space each term.

approvals.approved_version: The action points with owners and dates exactly as checked by the instructor in s5b, shared once with the team from the team page; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: colleagues keep e-mailing versions, so s4 keeps 85 (11.8); high: the shared space is used as assumed (16.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Agree office hour times with students, have students book a slot, advise and assist students in office hours, answer practical questions, and note agreements.

steps.what: Nursing instructor replies to students' e-mails to agree office hour times
Student confirms the office hour slot
Nursing instructor maintains office hours to advise and assist students
Nursing instructor answers repeated practical questions by e-mail
Nursing instructor notes agreements made with the student

tasks.design: Students book office hour slots themselves in the instructor's booking calendar ({CALENDAR}), so times are not agreed by e-mail. A course FAQ page in the learning environment ({LMS}) answers repeated practical questions on placements, deadlines and forms. Agreements are noted in the student file as today. Advising and assisting students stay with the instructor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Times were agreed by e-mail and the same practical questions came in every term.
tasks.enabler_now: Booking calendars and course FAQ pages are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Students in trouble rarely book a slot; they need to be approached.
tasks.human_edge: Noticing a student is thinking of quitting the programme.
tasks.altitude: Less e-mail about times and repeated questions; advising stays.

evidence.claim: Booking calendars let students pick slots; course FAQ pages answer repeated questions.

assumptions: Boundary: from the student's request to the advice notes; referral to the study adviser is outside.
Input contract: office hours set by the instructor; FAQ kept by the course team; fallback is e-mail.

Students pick a slot in about the time a reply took; their booking is shown in s2. s1 keeps 30 for changes; s4 keeps 60 for questions the FAQ does not answer; s5 is the first record of agreements and keeps its full time.
research_questions: Do practical questions by e-mail fall?

incremental.description: Nursing instructor updates the FAQ page each term.
Students look up the course FAQ page.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: half of the students still e-mail for times (s1 65) and few read the FAQ (s4 85) (7.3); high: booking and FAQ as assumed (16.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet mentees regularly, observe their teaching and give feedback, answer practical questions, share course materials, and plan mentoring meetings.

steps.what: Nursing instructor mentors junior and adjunct faculty members in regular meetings
Nursing instructor observes their teaching and gives feedback
Nursing instructor answers practical questions by e-mail
Nursing instructor e-mails course materials and templates
Nursing instructor plans mentoring meetings

tasks.design: An onboarding page for new and adjunct staff ({DOCS}) answers common questions on systems, rooms, placements and exam rules, and a shared course folder holds current materials and templates. Mentoring meetings recur in the calendar ({CALENDAR}). Mentoring talks and observing teaching stay with the instructor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Practical questions and materials went by e-mail one at a time.
tasks.enabler_now: Onboarding pages and shared folders are standard.
tasks.still_hard: Adjunct staff work at the hospital and are hard to reach.
tasks.human_edge: Helping a nurse who is new to teaching find their voice in front of a class.
tasks.altitude: Fewer repeated questions and mails; mentoring stays.

reach.learn: Whether the onboarding page cuts questions.

evidence.claim: Onboarding pages and shared course folders can answer common questions and hold materials.

assumptions: Boundary: from the new colleague's start to the meetings planned; formal teaching qualification is outside.
Input contract: onboarding page kept by the department office; fallback is e-mail.
Mentoring and observing do not change.
s3 keeps 50 for questions the onboarding page does not answer; s4 keeps 30 for pointing to the right file; s5 keeps 60 for moving meetings.
research_questions: Do mentees ask fewer practical questions?

incremental.description: Nursing instructor suggests missing answers for the onboarding page.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the onboarding page misses many local questions, so s3 keeps 80 (11.5); high: the page answers most questions as assumed (16.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Meet partner coordinators about programs and placements, exchange placement requests and student lists, track placement capacity per partner, draft cooperation agreements, check the final version, and send it for signature.

steps.what: Nursing instructor meets coordinators of hospitals, clinics and schools about training programs
Partner coordinators enter placement capacity in the portal
Nursing instructor prepares placement requests and student lists: in e-mails and spreadsheets today, in the shared placement portal after the change
Nursing instructor checks the final placement requests: students, periods and wards match the agreed capacity
Nursing instructor submits the checked placement requests to the partner in the portal
Nursing instructor tracks placement capacity per partner
Nursing instructor drafts or updates the cooperation agreement
Nursing instructor checks the final agreement with the partner: parties, places, duties and terms match what was agreed
Nursing instructor sends the checked agreement for signature: by post today, through electronic signature after the change

tasks.design: Hospitals, clinics and schools enter placement capacity and the school enters student requests in a shared placement portal ({PARTNER_PORTAL}), so lists are not e-mailed back and forth and capacity per partner shows on one screen; the instructor checks each request and submits it once. Cooperation agreements start from the legal team's template. Once the instructor has checked the final version with the partner, the instructor sends it for electronic signature ({ESIGN}). Meetings with partners stay with the instructor.
tasks.previous_blocker: Placement lists went back and forth as spreadsheets and agreements were posted for signature.
tasks.enabler_now: Placement portals and e-signature are common in nursing education.
tasks.still_hard: Each hospital has its own systems and contact people.
tasks.human_edge: Keeping a hospital on board when it is short of staff to mentor students.
tasks.altitude: Less list exchange; partner meetings stay.

evidence.claim: Shared placement portals and e-signature tools exist for education partnerships.

assumptions: Boundary: from program needs to the agreement sent; placing single students is outside.
Input contract: partners enter capacity in the portal; template from the legal team; fallback is spreadsheets and post.

Partners enter capacity in about the time an e-mail took; their entry is shown in s1b. s2 keeps 40 for preparing requests; checking and submitting them keep their full time; s3 keeps 40; s4 keeps 70; s6 keeps 30 for sending.
Meetings with partners do not change.
research_questions: Do double bookings and unfilled placements fall?

incremental.description: Nursing instructor reminds partners to update capacity.

approvals.approved_version: The cooperation agreement exactly as checked with the partner in s5, sent once for electronic signature to the partner's signatory; any change needs a new check.
The placement requests with students, periods and wards exactly as checked by the instructor in s2b, submitted once to the named partner in the placement portal; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: several partners do not keep capacity in the portal, so s2 keeps 70 and s3 keeps 80 (15.7); high: partners use the portal as assumed (26.4).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The nursing instructor keeps working with colleagues, advising students, mentoring and building partnerships; e-mail rounds, attachments and spreadsheet lists shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An instructor with more time for students and partners.
